conflicts.fact: Flame colour of chlorine isotopes (and chlorine itself)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says seawater/chlorine gives a single 'chlorine-family' colour with no specific colour, and only claims isotopes share the same colour. Lesson 5's model-building task has students write that both Cl isotopes 'would glow green in a flame test (copper-like)'. This asserts a specific colour for chlorine that is not established anywhere else and is scientifically unsupported.

conflicts.fact: Compound/substance that produces the violet flame (potassium source) and its relation to potassium
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 demonstrates potassium permanganate for the violet flame and the hearth story uses banana-peel ash. Lessons 3-9 treat the violet colour as potassium's, with no mention of permanganate. Lesson 1 also uses copper sulphate for a blue-green flame, while Lesson 6 has copper wire glowing green and Lesson 1 mentions steel wool. The substances differ across lessons for the same colour data.

conflicts.fact: When the student's initial model is revised and which element it tracks
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the initial sodium-atom drawing will be revised at the end of Lesson 3 (Bohr) and Lesson 7 (orbital model), and in Lesson 9. Lesson 7 says each learner was assigned a different element from H to Ca at Lesson 1, but Lesson 1 had every student draw a sodium atom. Lessons 3, 4, 6 and 8 also have varying elements/chosen elements.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering of prior knowledge / model layers
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says nucleus composition was added in Lessons 4–5, and Dalton's sphere in Lesson 1, whereas Lesson 1 only had a rough student drawing. Lesson 7 says its prior knowledge comes from Lessons 5–6 for energy levels and sublevels, though shells were introduced in Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson's sodium diagram is being built on
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 tells students to open their sodium diagram from Lesson 4, but the sodium Bohr diagram was created in Lesson 3 and Lesson 4's model revision could be on sodium, potassium or chlorine.

conflicts.fact: Hydrogen classified as Group 1 with 'similar flame colours' for Li, Na, K
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 lists H as Group 1 alongside Li, Na, K, and says Group 1 metals produce similar but distinct colours; yellow-orange and violet are quite different colours, and Lesson 3 says each element has a unique colour.
Lesson 4 exemplar uses 23Na and 24Na isotopes. Lesson 5 uses Na-23 (99.0%) and Na-22 (0.97%). Lesson 9 says Na-23 is the only stable isotope.
